cues.en: A few days ago, Facebook proudly announced that they'd achieved 8,000,000,000 video views a day.
cues.zh: 几天前，Facebook自豪地宣布，他们每天实现了80亿次视频观看。

cues.en: That's really impressive until you learn that in the first quarter of twenty fifteen, 725
cues.zh: 这确实令人印象深刻，直到你了解到在2015年第一季度，Facebook上1000个最受欢迎的视频中有725个

cues.en: of the thousand most viewed videos on Facebook were stolen, amassing a total of 17,000,000,000
cues.zh: 是被盗取的，总共累积了170亿

cues.en: views.
cues.zh: 次观看。

cues.en: Sites and content aggregators steal videos from YouTube to go viral on Facebook.
cues.zh: 网站和内容聚合器从YouTube盗取视频，在Facebook上疯传。

cues.en: These videos go viral because Facebook is cheating.
cues.zh: 这些视频之所以疯传，是因为Facebook在作弊。

cues.en: They rig their algorithm so that videos uploaded into their player are preferred to links because users should be kept as long as possible on the site so Facebook can show them as many ads as possible.
cues.zh: 他们操纵算法，使得上传到他们播放器中的视频比链接更受青睐，因为用户应尽可能长时间地留在网站上，以便Facebook向他们展示尽可能多的广告。

cues.en: This is after all their business model.
cues.zh: 毕竟这是他们的商业模式。

cues.en: But it also cheats when it comes to views. A view is counted after three seconds even if the video is muted.
cues.zh: 但在观看次数上，他们也在作弊。即使视频静音，观看三秒后也会被计为一次观看。

cues.en: Which means that because of autoplay, if you scroll through your timeline slowly enough, you count as a viewer.
cues.zh: 这意味着由于自动播放，如果你足够慢地滚动时间线，你也会被算作一个观众。

cues.en: That means engagement is terrible.
cues.zh: 这意味着参与度极差。

cues.en: Compared to YouTube views, Facebook views plummet after a few seconds because most views are not real.
cues.zh: 与YouTube的观看次数相比，Facebook的观看次数在几秒后就骤降，因为大多数观看并非真实。

cues.en: But large numbers are impressive, so Facebook keeps pretending.
cues.zh: 但大数字令人印象深刻，所以Facebook继续假装。

cues.en: While this forced virality is weird, the real problem is the so called freebooting,
cues.zh: 虽然这种强制病毒式传播很奇怪，但真正的问题是所谓的免费盗播，

cues.en: the stealing of videos.
cues.zh: 即盗取视频。

cues.en: Since Facebook prefers its own player, stolen videos reach way more people than the original.
cues.zh: 由于Facebook偏好自己的播放器，被盗视频触及的人数远超原创。

cues.en: Lately, this has happened to us more and more often. The most recent example amassed 3,200,000
cues.zh: 最近，这种情况越来越频繁地发生在我们身上。最近的例子在两天内累积了320万

cues.en: views and 140,000
cues.zh: 次观看和14万

cues.en: shares in two days, while our own post just reached 100,000 people and got shared 1,000 times.
cues.zh: 次分享，而我们自己的帖子仅触及10万人，被分享1000次。

cues.en: Other creators are hit even harder. Smarter Every Day's videos get stolen constantly, getting viewed up to 17,000,000
cues.zh: 其他创作者受到的打击更大。Smarter Every Day 的视频不断被盗，播放量最高达到 1700 万

cues.en: times. But even this is dwarfed by examples like Tyrese Gibson, a singer who steals viral videos like this one with 86,000,000
cues.zh: 次。但就连这也比不上 Tyrese Gibson 这样的例子：他是个歌手，会盗用像这个视频一样的爆款视频，该视频有 8600 万

cues.en: views on his Facebook page. He adds a link to buy his music too.
cues.zh: 次观看，就在他的 Facebook 主页上。他还加了购买他音乐的链接。

cues.en: He's not alone in this. A whole group of people have built their online presence around stealing other people's work.
cues.zh: 他不是唯一这么做的人。有一整群人靠盗用他人的作品来建立自己的网络影响力。

cues.en: This is really bad for independent creators.
cues.zh: 这对独立创作者来说非常糟糕。

cues.en: Contrary to popular belief, stolen content gives creators close to no exposure at all. Only The Thief and Facebook profit from this.
cues.zh: 与普遍看法相反，被盗内容几乎完全不会给创作者带来曝光。只有 The Thief 和 Facebook 从中获利。

cues.en: Quality content takes a lot of creativity,
cues.zh: 优质内容需要大量创造力，

cues.en: time, and love.
cues.zh: 时间，还有热爱。

cues.en: In our case, a single video literally takes hundreds of hours to make.
cues.zh: 对我们来说，做一条视频真的需要数百小时。

cues.en: Even we, with more than a million subscribers, are dependent on the ads and exposure.
cues.zh: 即便我们拥有超过一百万订阅者，也依赖广告和曝光。

cues.en: Without ads and the support of our generous patrons, we could not make videos.
cues.zh: 没有广告和慷慨赞助者的支持，我们就无法制作视频。

cues.en: For a small creator, a viral video can mean the difference between a career and a hobby. On YouTube, this kind of theft is not a problem because they have major safeguards that protect content from being stolen.
cues.zh: 对小创作者来说，一条爆款视频可能决定这是职业还是爱好。在 YouTube 上，这种盗用不成问题，因为他们有重要的保护措施，防止内容被盗。

cues.en: Although the Content ID system is far from perfect, especially for film critics and gamers,
cues.zh: 尽管 Content ID 系统远非完美，尤其是对影评人和游戏玩家来说，

cues.en: Facebook, on the other hand, pretends everything is fine and constantly announces one milestone after the other.
cues.zh: 另一方面，Facebook 却假装一切正常，还不断宣布一个又一个里程碑。

cues.en: But things are not fine. Let's look at the process of claiming your copyright on Facebook in the last year. One, get an email or tweet from a fan that gives you a direct link to your video.
cues.zh: 但事情并不美好。来看看过去一年在 Facebook 上主张版权的流程。第一，收到粉丝的邮件或推文，给你视频的直接链接。

cues.en: It's not possible to search for your videos on Facebook yourself. You depend on luck to find your stolen videos.
cues.zh: 你没法自己在 Facebook 上搜索自己的视频。能不能找到被盗视频全凭运气。

cues.en: Two, search for Facebook copyright infringement on Google because it's actually faster this way.
cues.zh: 第二，在 Google 上搜索 Facebook 版权侵权，因为这样其实更快。

cues.en: Three, fill out an annoyingly long contact form.
cues.zh: 第三，填写一张烦人的超长联系表单。

cues.en: Four, watch the views on your stolen videos rise.
cues.zh: 第四，看着你被盗视频的播放量上涨。

cues.en: Five, Facebook finally pulls the video. Conveniently,
cues.zh: 第五，Facebook 终于下架了视频。巧的是，

cues.en: the video has already gained 99%
cues.zh: 视频已经获得了 99%

cues.en: of all the views it will ever get. The thief doesn't have to fear any negative consequences at all.
cues.zh: 它最终能获得的全部播放量。小偷根本不用担心任何负面后果。

cues.en: This is what successful creators have to deal with constantly, and on top of losing out in terms of exposure and money, it just feels like a violation to be treated like that.
cues.zh: 成功创作者不得不一直面对这些；除了曝光和收入上的损失，被这样对待简直像是一种侵犯。

cues.en: In a recent statement, Facebook announced they want to change,
cues.zh: 在最近的一份声明中，Facebook 宣布他们想要改变，

cues.en: but it's hard to take them seriously when it still takes days for a stolen viral video to be taken down,
cues.zh: 但很难把他们当真，因为被盗的爆款视频仍要花好几天才能被下架，

cues.en: and Facebook does not share the profits made from it. At this point, Facebook is not a partner creators look forward to working with.
cues.zh: 而且 Facebook 不分享由此获得的利润。到了这个地步，Facebook 已不是创作者期待合作的伙伴。

cues.en: They've built their video empire on stolen content and disregard for original content creators.
cues.zh: 他们靠盗用内容和漠视原创内容创作者，建立起了自己的视频帝国。

cues.en: This is absolutely unacceptable for a corporation worth billions of dollars.
cues.zh: 对一家价值数十亿美元的公司来说，这绝对不可接受。

cues.en: Facebook is already testing various monetization models that will give the uploaders a cut of the ad revenue,
cues.zh: Facebook 已经在测试各种变现模式，让上传者分得一部分广告收入，

cues.en: which with the current state of play is troubling.
cues.zh: 但按照目前的情况，这令人担忧。

cues.en: Right now, this is mainly being tested with big media companies, but as creators, we don't feel like we're being asked or taken into consideration by the giant that is Facebook.
cues.zh: 目前，这主要还在与大型媒体公司进行测试，但作为创作者，我们感觉 Facebook 这个巨头并没有征求我们的意见，也没有考虑我们的处境。

cues.en: What can you, as a viewer, do to help here? If you spot stolen content on Facebook, make a comment linking to the original content. Alert the original creator because only they can file a copyright report.
cues.zh: 作为观众，你能做些什么来帮忙？如果你在 Facebook 上发现被盗用的内容，请发表评论并附上原始内容的链接。通知原作者，因为只有他们才能提交版权举报。

cues.en: Share this video or the one done by Smarter every day.
cues.zh: 分享这个视频，或者分享 Smarter Every Day 制作的那支视频。

cues.en: We all want the same thing. A free Internet that's the basis for creativity,
cues.zh: 我们都想要同一件事：一个自由的互联网，它是创造力的基础，

cues.en: community, and great stuff. We sincerely hope that Facebook will soon become a partner instead an obstacle to this goal.
cues.zh: 也是社群和优质内容的基础。我们真心希望 Facebook 很快能成为这一目标的伙伴，而不是阻碍。

cues.en: For more in-depth information, we recommend this article by Hank Green. And if you want to support us in our endeavor to survive in the world of online video and make more videos, you can do so on patreon.com.
cues.zh: 如果想了解更深入的信息，我们推荐 Hank Green 的这篇文章。如果你想支持我们，让我们继续在在线视频的世界里生存并制作更多视频，可以通过 patreon.com 支持我们。
